section.sectionSummaryBrief: The pleasure of transforming the public domain of separate mountains into a private domain, turning darkness into light, is the most sublime delight, akin to the laughter of Hashem when His children overcome Him.
section.t: Now, the pleasure
(desire)
that is above this, that a person transforms the public domain of the separate mountains into a private domain,
the transformation of darkness into light,
is the most sublime pleasure.
And as is known regarding laughter
[which is the matter of pleasure that comes specifically from something novel.
For similarly, so to speak, in the pleasure and laughter above,
it is from the novelty of transforming darkness into light60]
which is a greater pleasure than all other pleasures in the world61.
And it can be said that this is what they said62:
"Whoever teaches Torah to the son of an ignoramus, even the Holy One, blessed be He, decrees a decree and he nullifies it for his sake," as it is said63,
"And if you bring forth the precious from the vile, you shall be as My mouth."
For, behold, that the righteous one nullifies the decree of the Holy One, blessed be He64
(even though he knows that the Holy One, blessed be He, decreed it)
is because this itself is the will of the Holy One, blessed be He, that the righteous one nullify the decree, and the Holy One, blessed be He, has from this gratification and great pleasure65.
And in the manner of the saying of our Rabbis, may their memory be blessed66:
"What does the Holy One, blessed be He, do at that time?... He laughs and says, 'My children have defeated Me, My children have defeated Me,'"
for from this that "My children have defeated Me,"
there is produced above the greatest pleasure,
a smile and laughter.
And just as it is in matters of halachah,
that the Holy One, blessed be He, smiles and says, "My children have defeated Me, My children have defeated Me,"
so too is it regarding the ways of the world67,
the conduct in the world,
the decrees of the Holy One, blessed be He68,
that the Holy One, blessed be He, has gratification and great pleasure from this
[And in the manner of what our Rabbis, may their memory be blessed, said69
regarding the sanctification of the month: "You, even if you are deliberate,"
that even when they sanctified the month deliberately, contrary to the laws of the Torah, it is sanctified,
and
(even then)
the Holy One, blessed be He, says to the Heavenly Court, "I and you will go to the earthly court"70].
And this is: "Whoever teaches Torah to the son of an ignoramus... as it is said, 'And if you bring forth the precious from the vile, you shall be as My mouth,'"
for the pleasure and laughter above come from the service of refining the sparks,
to bring forth the precious from the vile,

and therefore, regarding one who teaches and disseminates Torah outside, even to the son of an ignoramus, they said, "The Holy One, blessed be He, decrees a decree and the righteous one nullifies it,"
for since from the service of this righteous one the pleasure and laughter above are produced, therefore the Holy One, blessed be He, decrees a decree and the righteous one nullifies it,
and the Holy One, blessed be He, laughs and says, "My children have defeated Me, My children have defeated Me."

section.sectionSummaryBrief: The concealments of the world are intended to enable the choice of life, empowering a person not to be disturbed by the world's impurity, as the very obstacles themselves can be transformed into a source of greater spiritual arousal.
section.t: And the above matter
(section 5)
—that the intention behind the concealments and veils of the world is so that it will be possible to have "and you shall choose life"—
gives strength and encouragement to a person not to be affected by seeing that the world is full of shells and the other side71,
a reality of a marketplace
(public domain)
in which there are rebels, and even that the rebels walk in it
(as above),
since this very fact that the world is in such a state is so that the person will overcome, etc.
And in the manner explained in the book Tzava'at HaRivash72,
that when a person prays with concentration and a gentile stands before him73
speaking and disturbing him in his prayer,
behold, this very thing should cause him to be aroused to pray with even more concentration from the depths of the heart.

For when he contemplates that the life-force of the gentile is the word of Hashem and the breath of His mouth, may He be blessed, which enlivens and brings him into being at this very moment when he speaks words that disturb the concentration of prayer,
and even that in these very words His speech, may He be blessed, is clothed in a state of exile,
behold, through this contemplation he will be aroused to pray with more concentration from the depths of the heart.
Not only is he not affected by the words of the gentile and prays as if he were not disturbing him,
but even more than this,
the very disturbance of the gentile causes him additional arousal.
For the sparks of holiness that were in exile in the words of the gentile are from a very high level
(therefore they fell to the lowest place),
and by the person extracting them from the shells,
to bring forth the precious from the vile,
their source, which is very high, is revealed in them,
and from this additional strength is drawn to the person in his service.
[And particularly according to what was explained above
(section 2)
regarding the matter of a descent for the sake of an ascent,
that the ascent after the descent is to a level more elevated than the level before the descent,
for similarly it is also regarding the ascent of the sparks,
that after the descent
(and the refinement)
they ascend to a level higher than they were in their source
(very high),
it can be said
that their ascent is even above the matter of "very high,"
and it is,
that through the service of refining the sparks, the intention is completed
(as above, section 4)
of a dwelling place for Him, may He be blessed, in the lower realms,
for Him, for His Essence,
for in His Essence, may He be blessed, no definition of above and below applies
(high and low)].
And analogous to the matter of "the destruction of the foot of the rebels,"
not only does he destroy and nullify the rebels
(rebels),
but he actually causes in them the matter of destruction74,
by refining the sparks within them and elevating them to their source.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: The two interpretations of "foot" are connected, as the refinement of the sparks of the impure foot is accomplished through the service of the three pilgrimage festivals, which correspond to the three lines of rectification and the three pillars upon which the world stands.
section.t: And based on this, the connection between the two interpretations of "foot" will also be understood
(from the marketplace),
that it refers to the foot of the other side
(the foot of the rebels),
and that it refers to the three pilgrimage festivals of holiness,
for the refinement and elevation of the sparks that are in the foot of the other side
(through which the matter of destruction is effected in it,
"the destruction of the foot of the rebels")
is through the service of the three pilgrimage festivals.
And the matter is that, behold, it is known75
the difference between Tohu and Tikkun,
that in Tohu the Sefiros were in the aspect of two lines, and in Tikkun they are in the aspect of three lines.
And the service of refining the sparks of Tohu that fell into the other side
(the foot of the rebels of the other side)
is by elevating them to the aspect of Tikkun, which is in three lines,
the matter of76
three pilgrimage festivals
(of holiness).
And in the service of man, this is the matter of the three pillars76
upon which the world stands77,
for man is a small world78,
and they are the standing of the entirety of the world—this physical, lower world, the lowest level of which there is none lower—
upon which all the worlds and the entire order of the chain of descent stand and are sustained.
And this is what is said regarding Yaakov
[And since the soul of Yaakov includes all souls79,
it is understood from this that similarly it is with every single Jew]
"And behold, Hashem was standing over him"80,
and our Rabbis, may their memory be blessed, said81,
"The righteous—their G-d is sustained upon them,"
that this matter of His G-dliness, may He be blessed, being in the aspect of "standing"
("standing" of a king82),
is sustained and stands, so to speak, upon our deeds and our service,
and particularly upon our deeds and our service during the time of exile83,
and even that through
(the refinement of)
the darkness of exile, this is brought about
("their G-d is sustained upon them"),
and even that this is brought about also through the service of a small finger84,
and as is known the ruling of the Rambam85,
that through one mitzvah
[whether in thought,
whether in speech, or whether in deed]
a person tips the scale of merit for himself and for the entire entire world, and causes salvation and deliverance for himself and for them.
